issues.legal_issue: A personal right of pre-emption is not transferable by itself to a third party.
material_facts: A decree granted relief on a pre-emption claim, and the decree-holder purported to assign rights connected with it to another person.
The court distinguished a transfer of the personal pre-emption right alone from a transfer of the decree-holder’s interest in the pre-emptional property.
issues.conclusion: The pre-emption right is personal and cannot, standing alone, be transferred to a third party.
issues.legal_principle: The purpose of pre-emption is to prevent strangers from acquiring an interest in property or entering the neighbourhood; transferring the personal right alone would defeat that purpose. The court referred to Mehr Khan v. Gulam Rasul, AIR 1922 Lahore 300; Negeshwar v. Taluk Singh, AIR 1930 Oudh 195; Wajid Ali v. Salian, [1909] ILR 31 An 623; Zila Singh v. Hazari, [1979] 3 SCR 222; Chandrup Singh v. Data Ram, AIR 1983 P & H 1; Sarju Prasad v. Jamna Prasad; and Jugal Kishore Saraj v. Raw Cotton Co. Ltd., [1955] SCR 1369.

predicates.preemption_proceeding: A claimant seeks to acquire property by exercising a right of pre-emption.
predicates.transfer_to_third_party: The holder purports to transfer the right to someone else.
predicates.assignment_only_transfers_personal_preem: The transfer conveys only the personal pre-emption right and not an interest in the pre-emptional property.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption claimant transfers only the personal right to a third party, that right is not transferable.

issues.legal_issue: An assignee may execute a pre-emption decree where the assignment transfers the decree-holder’s interest in the pre-emptional property, rather than merely the personal right, and the decree-holder has complied with the decree’s payment condition.
material_facts: A pre-emption decree required the successful claimant to deposit the sale price by a specified deadline.
The High Court found that the decree-holder had taken timely steps to pay, but administrative difficulties delayed the deposit; it treated the deposit as timely.
The assignment document showed an intention to transfer the decree-holder’s interest in the pre-emptional land, not merely the decree while title remained with the decree-holder.
The document required the assignee to seek substitution in the pending execution proceedings and then obtain possession.
The assignee was substituted as decree-holder after notice to the judgment-debtor.
issues.conclusion: The assignee was entitled to execute the decree and obtain possession of the land.
issues.legal_principle: A personal pre-emption right cannot be assigned as a bare right, but the court found that the assignment transferred the decree-holder’s interest in the pre-emptional property. Section 146 and Order XXI Rule 16 of the Code of Civil Procedure were relevant to execution by a person claiming under the decree-holder, while Order XX Rule 14 concerns the decree’s payment condition. The court referred to Mehr Khan v. Gulam Rasul, AIR 1922 Lahore 300; Negeshwar v. Taluk Singh, AIR 1930 Oudh 195; Wajid Ali v. Salian, [1909] ILR 31 An 623; Zila Singh v. Hazari, [1979] 3 SCR 222; Chandrup Singh v. Data Ram, AIR 1983 P & H 1; Sarju Prasad v. Jamna Prasad; and Jugal Kishore Saraj v. Raw Cotton Co. Ltd., [1955] SCR 1369.

rule.if: preemption_decree_execution and decree_holder_took_timely_steps_to_meet_payment_condition and administrative_obstacles_delayed_deposit and assignment_transferred_property_interest_not_merely_decree and assignee_was_substituted_after_notice

predicates.preemption_decree_execution: A person seeks to execute a decree granting relief on a pre-emption claim.
predicates.decree_holder_took_timely_steps_to_meet_: The successful claimant took timely steps to make the payment required by the decree.
predicates.administrative_obstacles_delayed_deposit: Administrative difficulties, rather than the claimant’s inaction, delayed the actual deposit.
predicates.assignment_transferred_property_interest: The assignment conveyed the decree-holder’s interest in the pre-emptional property rather than a bare decree with that interest remaining vested in the decree-holder.
predicates.assignee_was_substituted_after_notice: The assignee was substituted as decree-holder in the execution proceeding after notice to the judgment-debtor.

issues.definition: An assignee may execute a pre-emption decree when the claimant took timely steps to satisfy its payment condition, administrative obstacles delayed the deposit, the assignment transferred the property interest, and the assignee was substituted after notice.
